Summarize the following draft in five sentences, then list its three main claims.

# What It Takes to Run a 125B LLM Fast on a 64 GB Mac, and How to Go Faster

*How batch-invariant speculative checks, SSD-streamed experts and a certified lossy layer build on each other within a
45 GB memory line, and what each piece adds.*

Kamen Levi

Independent researcher

---

## 0. Draft status (delete before release)

- **v3-draft, Sun 8 Nov 2026, 19:5x (Mon 9 Nov 00:4x: chat as shipped with PF-D; Strata's file; DFlash2's source;
  09:5x: the number check's first pass applied, 22 items; gates end 16:00; 10:3x: lossy rows re-based on CERT / L /
  L + COH, the shipped L + COH passed its card gate; 11:5x: frozen for the 12:00 full draft, open items in Appendix A).
  Dates: `MONDAY.md`** (full draft Mon 12:00; number check and related-work check
  12:00-16:00; finals 18:00; the release happens only on the project owner's word). Since v2: every open item of
  sections 4-8 is filled or turned into a stated limit (Appendix A), section 12 is re-opened, and the abstract's ratios
  are like for like. Sections 9-10 aligned with STYLE.md (Sun 20:3x); Appendix F is a summary; its full form is [KERNELS] 4.4 and 6.3-6.5. v1.1 is
  kept as `MAIN_v1.1_2026-11-06.md`.
- **The set.** This paper is [MAIN]. The companions are [SMALL-RAM], [KERNELS], [EVAL], [DRAFTER] and [RELEASE]; their
  shared words and metrics are in `STYLE.md`. Kernels, the certification method, the 32 / 24 / 12 GB lines and the drafter
  are told in full there and summarised here.
- **Marks.** [K] measured, [P] priced, [G] judgement; the mark travels with the number. `[[TBD-n]]` = not measured yet.
- **Speeds** are the STYLE.md triple: whole decode, whole request, first token, plus the lifetime peak, pooled over the
  named prompt set. The engine's run reports quote a geometric mean over prompts ("geo"), 0-8 % higher; both are in
  Appendix E (`MoonShots/papers/main_table.txt`, re-derived from the raw run records by `papers/main_table.py`).
- **Checked for this version:** every number in sections 6-7 was re-read from the file named beside it on Sun 8 Nov
  (16:5x-19:5x), and the headings were checked for WITHDRAWN / CORRECTED. Section 8's rows and section 12's identifiers
  were re-opened on Sun 8 Nov (`MoonShots/research/relwork`, passes 1 and 2a); pass 2 (the companions' references,
  issue figures, community posts) runs Mon 12:00-16:00. Competitor numbers are self-reported unless we reproduced them.

### Outline (v2)
- Abstract.
- 1 Introduction: the setting, contributions, what we do not claim, the companion papers.
- 2 Definitions and how we measure: exact (to which reference), lossy with same scores (on which benchmarks), gate open;
  the speed triple; pooled aggregation; the four 12-prompt sets; marks and sources.
- 3 Exactness (short; [KERNELS] has the kernels): the definition, the references REF2 -> NAX6-N, the audits (36 prompts;
  E5 96 / 96; chat and math 24 / 24; chat after the coherent-read fix 12 / 12), changing a reference.
- 4 The 45 GB system: model, store and SSD; cache and loader; the check loop; the exact default and its levers (new: cache
  keep, wired limit, the exact-safe bundle, coherent reads, the 1-row check); prefill (layer-major, exact); the memory line
  and where it is exceeded (agent prompts, 45.1 GB).
- 5 The lossy configuration and its certificate (short; [EVAL] has the method): its parts; CERT (same scores on
  HumanEval+, MBPP, math and IFEval, both orders); chat is lossy, not exact; the chat lever M1-B and its open gate.
- 6 Results: the 45 GB tables (exact, lossy-certified, chat gate open), prefill, and where a request's time goes.
- 7 Same machine, same prompts: Strata (decode, whole request, first token; equal memory; break-even; caveats).
- 8 Published runs and related work (re-checked Sun 8 and Mon 9 Nov; every row self-reported unless we reproduced it).
- 9 Methods that carry to other models (the SSD wake penalty and keepalive; 3-bit kept experts on drafted rows; relaxed
  acceptance restricted to code comments).
- 10 Negative results and corrected headlines (the steady metric; 157.9 and 40.8 withdrawn; larger prefill chunks change
  logits; never-wait; split; CD16; trellis; ...).
- 11 What we left on the table.
- 12 References. Appendices: A open items, B figures, C how the results were produced and the code release (GPL-3, MLX
  0.32.2 + pad to 64), D ledger keys, E every row (pooled and geo, per pass).

---

## Abstract

We run a 125B-parameter mixture-of-experts model (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 48 layers, 512 routed experts per layer, 10 per
token) on one MacBook Pro (M5 Pro, 18-core CPU, 20-core GPU, 64 GB, 2 TB SSD), with the routed experts streamed from the internal SSD at about 3.2
bits per weight and the process's lifetime peak at most 45 GB on the benchmark prompts (plus a 7.45 GB expert tier that
macOS may reclaim; longer prompts go over it, section 6.1). The
pieces are mostly published; this paper is about how they depend
on each other and what each adds. Speculative decoding pays one pass of the large model for up to 16 drafted tokens, but
it is exact only if that pass computes the same bits as one-token decoding. Batch-invariant kernels on the GPU and its
matrix units make it so, and we audit it on every run (96 of 96 code runs, 24 of 24 chat and 24 of 24 math runs
token-identical to one-token greedy decoding). Exactness then turns every later optimisation into a test of token
equality that takes minutes: the levers of the streamed engine, such as per-layer expert pools and expert reads
hidden behind the GPU's work, were each adopted that way. On top of the exact engine, a lossy layer
lets drafted rows of code answers skip cold experts and run 3-bit parts, and ships only if it scores the same as the
exact reference on the model's benchmarks.

The exact configuration decodes 101.4 tok/s on 12 HumanEval prompts, 70.4 on 12 MBPP, 77.9 on 12 math and 37.1 on 12
chat (IFEval) prompts, at a lifetime peak of 41.7-42.5 GB [K]. The lossy configuration we ship scores the same as the
exact reference on the model card's IFBench, GPQA Diamond and LiveCodeBench v6 in both prompt orders, and decodes 164.0,
112.7, 78.9 and 45.2 tok/s on the same sets at 42.4-43.2 GB [K]. Our first token is slow, a median of 2.7-4.6 s on these
short prompts: on the same machine and prompts the open engine Strata's takes 0.54-1.01 s, and Strata wins or ties every
